findings.title: NetworkPolicy allows a Service's cluster IP, which policies never see
findings.cause: container client exits because its connection to Service web times out: NetworkPolicy client-egress allows egress to ipBlock 10.96.0.200/32, which holds the Service's cluster IP 10.96.0.200, but a policy is checked after the Service has forwarded the connection, against the pods' IPs, such as 10.244.0.99, which no rule allows; a blocked connection is dropped, not refused; its log says: "wget: download timed out"; Deployment client has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container client exited with code 1 (Error), restarted 6 times
last lines of container client's log (current run)
evidence.detail:
Connecting to web (10.96.0.200:80)
wget: download timed out

evidence.what: NetworkPolicy client-egress allows egress to ipBlock 10.96.0.200/32
evidence.command: kubectl get networkpolicy client-egress -n kd-networkpolicy-service-cluster-ip -o jsonpath='{.spec.egress}'
kubectl get service web -n kd-networkpolicy-service-cluster-ip -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}'

findings.fix: In NetworkPolicy client-egress, replace the ipBlock with a podSelector for the Service's pods (app=web) on port 8080, the pods' port: an ipBlock is for addresses outside the cluster, and a policy never sees a Service's cluster IP.
